items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Well, when I was playing with him, we had Buddy Petit... I can picture the band on the bandstand in the Economy Hall.

ctx.x: Pajot played out there too. Mm-hmm. He had a band out there. But not with Henry Martin, a different time? No, I don't think, I don't think. No. No. Because that was before Pajot's time, you know, see, I imagine. Oh yeah. What about Buddy Petit? Did you remember who played with him much?

Well, when I was playing with him, we had Buddy Petit, and we had all trombone with us. We had Buddy Manatee, we had Zeb Lennaris, and we had Simon the Wild on bass. And he had clarinet, and Zeb Lennaris on clarinet, on trombone. Morris Francis with a René in attire. I can picture the band on the bandstand in the Economy Hall. Hmm. But I can't picture the trombone playing.
And who'd you say was a guitar player, a banjo player? Buddy Manatee. Buddy Manatee and Simon. And Simon. And no piano, of course. No. No violin. No. No.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: I knew of him, you know, see.

ctx.x: I just remember who was playing with him. I don't know who had the band, did you hear? No, I don't remember all that.

Now Pete could tell you, yeah, he could tell you just who was playing out there. But he used to lay off from there on Sunday night, Saturday, Sunday, or Monday night, and play with Ory. See, he played with that band and played with Ory's band at that time, and I knew of him, you know, see. That was around 1917, 1918. Frankie Dewson played out there a good while, and I don't know whether he was playing with Frankie Dewson or not. See, he could have been. Frankie played with the manager of the band out there.
It must have been the Eagle or something.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Me, Badlacks, Lewis Givens, Poire. Went there two nights a week... I played there them two nights.

ctx.x: The famous two. Me, Badlacks, Lewis Givens, Poire. Went there two nights a week. See, them boys was playing there, you know. And Smiley and Joe and Thed O, they were playing one night, you see. I mean, they were playing there all the week. Monday night, the white band would be off. And Sunday night, Thed O and them would be off with Badlacks. I played there them two nights. Played there for about a year. And then I went with, with, uh, uh, uh, O'Vell Anderson's rock and roll band. I played with them about two or…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I think I was playing with, I think I was playing with, Buddy Petit, when I went to Los Angeles.

ctx.x: Who were you working with then? Before you went with him?
Before I went to Los Angeles, I think I was playing with, I think I was playing with, Buddy Petit, when I went to Los Angeles. I went to Los Angeles the year of 1919.

I remember Fass tells about going out there, that he helped organize the group here to go out. That's right. And I know he said he picked up some of the fellows were working out there at Walter Dacu's, maybe at the bungalow out near the lake. Must have been. You weren't in that band though, Walter and Mutt and Wade Whaley, you weren't working with them. No, that's who went with us, Wade Whaley.
